title: The remote desktop Papa stopped using
story: In 2021 Bunty set up remote desktop on the accounts PC so Papa could approve bills from Lonavala. Papa uses an app now. The door is still open.
fix: Turn remote desktop off. If someone truly needs it, put it behind a VPN with MFA.

title: The folder called CLIENTS
story: The CLIENTS folder is shared with 'Everyone' so the new trainee could find a quotation. 'Everyone' turned out to include the guest Wi-Fi.
fix: Share the folder with the people who need it, and nobody else.

title: Cousin Pinku's CCTV upgrade
story: Pinku made the shop cameras viewable 'from anywhere'. From anywhere, it turns out, means from anywhere.
fix: Remove the port forwarding on the router. View cameras through the vendor's app or a VPN instead.

title: The router the installer left open
story: The installer turned on remote admin 'just for setup'. Setup was three Diwalis ago.
fix: Switch off router admin from the internet. Manage it only from inside the office.

title: The billing database that never asked
story: The billing software's database answers anyone on the network, no questions asked. It's very polite.
fix: Set a password on the database and let only the billing PC connect to it.

title: Chintu's 2019 website test
story: Under the stairs, a small box from Chintu's website experiment is still switched on, still answering, still nobody's job.
fix: Switch off and remove what nobody uses. Unknown means unowned.

title: The supplier upload folder
story: Suppliers upload invoices by FTP with no login. So can anyone else who finds it.
fix: Turn off anonymous FTP. Use a shared link that needs a login, or email.

title: The printer that runs the office
story: The printer's settings page opens for anyone on the network. Last month someone renamed it 'Bunty's Printer'.
fix: Restrict the printer's admin page to your IT person.

title: Three devices nobody can name
story: A network scan found three devices nobody could identify. One was the neighbour's smart TV.
fix: Know every device on your network. Remove what doesn't belong.

title: One Wi-Fi for everyone
story: Guests, customers and the accounts PC all share one Wi-Fi network. Very hospitable. Very flat.
fix: Put guests on a separate network so they can't reach your office devices.
